Syncly.subtitle: Developer Networking Platform
Syncly.description: Developer-to-developer networking platform built solo end to end. Members pick a mentorship role (mentor, learner, both), swipe a paginated feed of developers they have not met (Vibe to connect, Ghost to pass); the recipient replies Link or Noped, and a mutual Link unlocks real-time 1:1 chat over Socket.IO with persisted history. Each member gets a shareable portfolio page at their slug (projects, experience, education, certifications, theme, SEO, visibility). httpOnly JWT cookie auth with bcrypt; AWS SES email on every swipe plus a daily 08:00 node-cron reminder for pending Vibes. Loop: Discover → Vibe → Link → Chat → Showcase.

GlycanBench: a unified resource for work.subtitle: Glycoinformatics Web Server + Python Package · SASTRA University

Explainable Machine Learning-Based Appro.subtitle: M.Tech Thesis · Explainable AI · Drug Discovery
Explainable Machine Learning-Based Appro.description: Vigneshwaran's M.Tech thesis developing an explainable ML framework to identify potent EGFR inhibitors for ovarian cancer. EGFR is a key therapeutic target — its overexpression drives uncontrolled cancer cell proliferation. 310 compounds sourced from ChEMBL (EGFR Target ID: CHEMBL3009) were encoded with RDKit and Mordred molecular descriptors (1833 → 179 features via LASSO selection). Six classifiers evaluated: Gradient Boosting (98.47% accuracy, AUC=1.00), Random Forest (98.28%, AUC≈1.00), SVM (AUC=0.99), Logistic Regression, KNN, Naive Bayes. SHAP force and waterfall plots identified key activity-driving descriptors: PEOE_VSA9, SM_VSA10, fr_bicyclic, BCUT2D_MRLOW. Binary classification: Active (IC50 ≤ 1000 nM) vs Inactive (IC50 ≥ 10000 nM).

Prediction of lignocellulosic components.subtitle: ML for Green Energy · Biomass Pretreatment
Prediction of lignocellulosic components.description: This study explores efficient bioethanol production from waste biomass using an integrated approach of nanotechnology, green pretreatment methods, and machine learning. Twenty different lignocellulosic biomass samples (mainly fruit peels and agro-wastes) were pretreated using physical, chemical, and novel physicochemical methods — including nanocatalyst-assisted ionic liquid combined with ultrasound — to extract fermentable sugars. Iron nanoparticles synthesised from Musa acuminata peels improved biomass breakdown. Machine learning models — Decision Tree, Random Forest, and LGBM — were trained on experimental data to predict biomass composition and ethanol yield. Random Forest and Decision Tree showed high accuracy in predicting lignocellulosic content and sugar yield. A BFuel web platform was developed to store and display experimental data.
key_contributions: Eco-friendly biomass pretreatment using nanotechnology and ionic liquids
Multiple ML algorithms for predictive modeling of biomass composition and ethanol yield
BFuel web-based database for managing biomass and bioethanol data

QSPR for Posaconazole SEDDS.subtitle: Drug Solubility Prediction · Manipal Institute of Technology
QSPR for Posaconazole SEDDS.description: Developed at Manipal Institute of Technology (supervised by Dr. Neha Sureshchandra Gandhi) as part of a research internship. Built ML-based QSPR models to predict Posaconazole solubility in Self-Emulsifying Drug Delivery Systems (SEDDS). Dataset consisted of oils, surfactants, co-surfactants, and drug compositions. 50+ molecular descriptors generated with RDKit; VIF analysis reduced to 10 key descriptors: ELUMO, EHOMO, MaxQ-, MaxQ+, MinPartialCharge, MaxPartialCharge, MinAbsPartialCharge, FpDensityMorgan2, PEOE_VSA1, HallKierAlpha. Random Forest achieved R²=0.865, outperforming PLS (0.733), Linear Regression (0.740), SVM (0.630), and KNN (0.590).

Suitability Studies Of Fruits Of West In.subtitle: Biofuel Feedstock Evaluation
Suitability Studies Of Fruits Of West In.description: Investigated the potential of Guazuma ulmifolia (West Indian Elm) fruits as a feedstock for biofuel production. Fruits were ground into powder and extracted using solvent extraction with petroleum ether. Confirmatory tests for lipids (emulsion and acrolein assays) were performed on the solvent-vaporised residue. The processed biomass was subjected to H₂SO₄ acid hydrolysis followed by heat treatment and tested for fermentable sugars. The sample contained no lipids but did contain carbohydrates, supporting bioethanol potential over biodiesel. Future work focuses on comparative analysis of solvent extraction versus nano-catalysts and enzymatic pretreatment for improved sugar yield.
Suitability Studies Of Fruits Of West In.findings: No lipids detected; carbohydrates confirmed — supports bioethanol over biodiesel pathway
